Resolves #2334
Refs #15000

Adds `Neo.calendar.view.month.EventDragZone` and `Neo.calendar.view.month.plugin.DragDrop` so events in the calendar month view (`Neo.calendar.view.month.Component`) can be dragged across `.neo-day` cells while preserving their local time-of-day and duration.

Evidence: L3 (Playwright real-pointer browser e2e test in `test/playwright/e2e/rendering/CalendarMonthEventDrag.spec.mjs` dragging `.neo-event.neo-draggable` across `.neo-day` cells via `page.mouse`, plus unit suite in `test/playwright/unit/calendar/MonthView.spec.mjs`) → L3 required.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Dragging an event into a different day in `calendar.view.month.Component` moves the event to that day while preserving start time and duration | `src/calendar/view/month/EventDragZone.mjs:11-235`, `src/calendar/view/month/plugin/DragDrop.mjs:9-148`, `src/calendar/view/month/Component.mjs:35-653`, `resources/scss/src/calendar/view/month/Component.scss:59-66`, `test/playwright/e2e/rendering/CalendarMonthEventDrag.spec.mjs:1-54` (red at `ac87e664a3`, green at `f5104b6cb8`), `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs:50`, `test/playwright/unit/calendar/MonthView.spec.mjs:359-519` (5/5 passing) |

## Deltas from ticket
None. Contract Ledger posted in [`#2334` comment `IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABjXTGzQ`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/2334#issuecomment-6668207821).

## Test Evidence
All coverage runs in CI (`test/playwright/e2e/rendering/CalendarMonthEventDrag.spec.mjs` and `test/playwright/unit/calendar/MonthView.spec.mjs`).

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] None required; covered by CI `e2e-engine` and `unit` suites on `dev`.

# PR Review Summary

**Status:** Request Changes

*Cycle-1 reviewers: run the §0 premise catalog BEFORE any defect audit. A firing row ends the review at one premise Required Action — **Drop+Supersede** by default — never an iteration list.*

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

Per §9 Strategic-Fit Step-Back:
- **Decision**: Request Changes
- **Rationale**: No premise row fires. #2334 asks for exactly this, and the PR builds it on the week view's own primitives. But the delivered feature cannot be used with a real pointer: month events never carry the class the drag sensor arms on, so no drag starts. The repair is one class plus the proof that was missing, so this is an in-place repair, not a scope transfer or a restart.

**Peer-Review Opening:** Thanks, Maryam. This is a clean port of a feature that has waited since 2022. Resolving the drop target from the `.neo-day` under the pointer, instead of from 7-column geometry, is the right call: it holds with `showWeekends: false`, with any `weekStartDay`, and with the month headers that sit between week rows. One class stands between this and a working drag. I proved that in a real browser, and the details are below.

---

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #2334 (a feature request, so there is no `Design authority:` line to check); the changed-file list; `dev`'s `src/calendar/view/month/Component.mjs` (`createWeek`, the `bind` block, `showWeekends`/`weekStartDay`); the week view's drag stack (`week/EventDragZone.mjs`, `week/plugin/DragDrop.mjs`, `week/Component.mjs` `afterSetEnableDrag` l.363–391 and the event `cls` at l.909); the main-thread sensor (`src/main/draggable/sensor/Base.mjs` l.23, `Mouse.mjs` l.135); and `src/draggable/DragZone.mjs` zone registration (l.211, l.228).
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** Mirror the week view. An `enableDrag_` config bound to `data.events.enableDrag` lazily loads a month `DragDrop` plugin, and that plugin creates a month `EventDragZone`. The event nodes carry `neo-draggable`, so the sensor arms on them. The drop target comes from the `.neo-day` under the pointer, which keeps 7 columns, uniform row height and scroll offset out of the code (month headers interleave and `showWeekends: false` leaves 5 columns). Proof is a real-pointer e2e: a unit spec that calls the handlers directly can't see the sensor gate.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Partly matches. **Improves** target resolution: `dragMove` walks `targetPath` to the `.neo-day`, and `createWeek` now stamps that day's date as its `flag`. **Contradicts** the expected shape on drag admission: the event node's `cls` is still `['neo-event', 'neo-<color>']`, and `git grep neo-draggable` over `src/calendar` at `ac87e664a3` hits only the week view. The reviewer falsifier below turns that static reading into a measured red and a measured green.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres. A 2022 operator ticket from the #15000 premise sweep ships through the week view's existing primitive (the same plugin and zone pattern, the same state-provider flag) rather than a parallel mechanism.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: The unit spec drives `plugin.onEventDragStart/Move/End` directly, so it skips the one gate that decides whether a drag exists: the main thread's `testPathInclusion(event, ['neo-draggable', 'neo-resizable'])`. That is how a green L2 suite ships a feature no user can trigger. A second, smaller watch item: `dragEnd` commits with `record.setSilent`, so no `recordChange` fires, and other consumers of the shared events store don't learn the event moved. The week view does the same, so this is inherited (hypothesis — needs V-B-A before implementation), not a defect of this PR.
